summary: M0 model-only verdict: ESCALATE @ 0.65. l.duman@aegean.edu shows a stable months-long baseline of twice-daily logins from Manisa, Turkey (university AS-AEGEAN-EDU in the mornings on DEV-H06-L; TTNET AS9121 evenings on DEV-H06-P with MFA). Starting 2026-10-10, authentications suddenly appear from Athens, Greece (Vodafone-panafon AS3329) on new devices DEV-H06-P/DEV-H06-T, including MFA-approved events and several "success" logins with mfa_prompt_count=0 from the new country/devices. There are zero mail events to check for inbox rules, forwarding, or other post-compromise activity, and no data to confirm whether the travel is legitimate. This is not confirmed account takeover (MFA was passed, no malicious mail activity observed), not benign (geography/device change unexplained), and stronger than a weak signal given repeated successful remote-country authentications involving MFA. Insufficient evidence and potential exposure warrant human review (verify travel, inspect device registration, review full mail/audit logs before containing).
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
